chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Ziyād al-Khazzāz, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the woman with istiḥāḍah: what should she do when she sees blood, and when she sees yellow discharge, and how long should she leave the salat (prayer)? He said: The minimum of menstruation is three [days] and its maximum is ten, and she combines between the two salats (prayers).

key_terms.الدَّمَ: blood seen by the woman in the context of determining her ruling
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: salat (prayer), which may be left or performed according to the ruling
key_terms.الصَّلَاتَيْنِ: the two salats (prayers) that are to be combined
key_terms.الصُّفْرَةَ: yellow discharge relevant to the legal assessment of bleeding
key_terms.الْحَيْضِ: menstruation with its legally defined duration
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةِ: a woman experiencing istiḥāḍah, irregular non-menstrual bleeding
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةٌ: the minimum number of days for menstruation
key_terms.عَشَرَةٌ: the maximum number of days for menstruation

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum and maximum length of menstruation, and how does a woman with istiḥāḍah perform salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the woman experiencing istiḥāḍah and the distinction related to menstrual duration. It states that the minimum period of hayd is three days and the maximum is ten, and indicates that she combines the two salats (prayers).
